title: Overwriting an existing PCK/ZIP fails silently if the file you're overwriting is locked
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.6.2 and previous versions of 4.x

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable (89cea1439) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Single-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-14900KF (32 threads) - 63.83 GiB memory

### Issue description

When you press "Export PCK/ZIP..." and choose to overwrite an existing file, and that file is locked, it won't overwrite the file and fail silently. This happens quite often as I am developing a game where the main game loads specific modules (as PCK files). If you leave the game running while doing the export, those PCK files will be locked.

At a minimum I would expect a warning message (dialog popping up) to inform the user that overwriting the file failed with an "OK" button to confirm. After confirming I would expect to go back to the "Export" window (that should still be open).

This dialog can be extended with a "Retry" button to allow the user to unlock the file (by quitting the game) and trying again. That would speed up the process of trying again. In this case the "OK" button should be renamed to "Cancel".

Note that right now if you select an existing file, you also get a dialog to confirm you want to overwrite that file. That is still fine. It might be possible to also do a check at that point to see if the file is locked, but it's debatable if that is sufficient as you are really checking too early (the file might unlock later, or reversely be locked later, so this check would have to be done again anyway when really overwriting the file).

### Steps to reproduce

See above.
